pos.personaBrief: Goal says his Flamengo pressed without the ball and then dominated possession; Trivela notes patient ball work and a compact team. He wanted the ball and the initiative, not a reactive side.

pro.personaBrief: Trivela (verified) says a failed move on one side meant returning the ball to the defense and restarting the other way, with no aimless crosses. But he also used ponto futuro, rehearsed long balls (Andrade to Nunes) and Zico's 'second punch' quick-kill idea.

est.personaBrief: Total-football and basketball-style 'participação total', polivalência and overlapping point to fluid roles with players close to the play. 'Marcação por setor' and tactical drilling without opposition add defined structure.

lar.personaBrief: Trivela: wingers cut inside and the full-back overlaps through the open corridor; in the 1978 Carioca final Flamengo held the full-backs and attacked more through the middle. Coutinho favored central, crowded midfields (polivalentes, Chicão over Falcão), not classic wingers.

blo.personaBrief: Trivela: compact teams with high marking lines, pressing from the start; Goal: Flamengo pressed without the ball. His 'participação total' includes the shooter helping to mark at once.

mar.personaBrief: The only marking label found is 'marcação por setor' (Trivela, verified), a zone-style concept he introduced to Flamengo. No evidence of dedicated man-markers.

pla.personaBrief: He arrived with a ready modern model and drilled it daily, including the opponent's scheme explained in training (Nunes). He still adapted at the 1978 World Cup (aerial play on a bad pitch), but his core was his own idea.

res.personaBrief: 'Campeões morais' shows he valued how the team played even without the title. His attacking, massacre-the-opponent Flamengo and pressure to the end suggest no settling for draws or shutting games down.

sis.personaBrief: He demanded 'participação total', with the shooter defending and no player who only attacks. He relied on drilled collective movement and tactical discipline (Nunes), while still having Zico.

jog.personaBrief: He was a fitness scientist (Cooper method, NASA) who demanded physical intensity, but also daily fundamentals work (Júnior). He chose Chicão over Falcão and fielded bigger players like Roberto Dinamite, though he regretted leaving out technical Júnior.

bas.personaBrief: Trivela (verified): he took the Flamengo youngsters (Zico, Júnior, Adílio, Andrade, Tita) and mixed them with experienced players (Carpegiani, Raul, Ramires). Home-grown core, but veterans anchored the title runs.

lid.personaBrief: He kept open dialogue with the players (Trivela) and was seen as a leader, but yielded to the CBD president in 1978 and was criticized for lacking firmness. His discipline came through professionalism and tactical demands.
